blocks.text: Aztec and Inca arrangements were not structurally identical empires. Urban alliances and tribute in one case, and roads, labor obligations, storage and nodes in the other, must be understood within their environments. Large-scale political capability could be assembled differently.

A center's mobilizing power did not mean every locality related to it in the same way. Local interests, internal relationships and existing conflicts shaped cooperation, resistance and the reorganization of power under external shock.

blocks.caption: Inca Tawantinsuyu · Context illustration; historical interpretation is in the text.

blocks.text: Rapid conquest cannot be explained solely by the number of outsiders or one weapon. Disease, alliances, political structures and the loss of central control interacted. Reducing this process to civilizational superiority hides the different groups involved.

The loss of a center did not end resistance, government or social continuity. Political rupture and long-term colonial integration were distinct processes. Key wartime events must be distinguished from subsequent changes instead of compressing everything into one moment.
